newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: World Bank report says Slovak policy EU barrier.
newsitem.headline: World Bank report says Slovak policy EU barrier.

text.p: Uncertainty over the Slovakia's policy to allow foreign participation in the privatisation of strategic companies, including banks, could prevent its entry to the European Union, a World Bank report said.

"In developing an industrial policy for Slovakia, some government statements, policies, and actions appear to contradict...open and fair competition and thus can be a barrier to early accession to the EU," the report said.

The report said these contradictory moves included preference shown for domestic investors in the second wave of privatisation and alleged close ties between the new owners of enterprises and the government.

Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's cabinet has been widely criticised for a number of selloffs of state property by the National Property Fund (NPF), the privatisation agency controlled by the ruling coalition.
Since 1994, the NPF has directly sold off state property worth some 100 billion crowns often well under the market price.
Slovakia should "take steps to reduce the foreign perception that the government favors domestic companies and investors in privatisation and in its industrial policies," the report said.
"This image of Slovak industrial policy, whether valid or not, is probably one of the obstacles to EU accession," it added.
The government should support an increase in the flow of foreign capital, which could contribute to modernisation and expansion of Slovak enterprises, the report said.
The report noted that post-Communist foreign direct investment into Slovakia has lagged behind its neighbours, totalling $845 million between January 1990 and September 1996.
